account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, Bret Peters, a father and former state trooper, was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 mph came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. TeslaCam footage, aired by Fox 46 Charlotte and described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving into the right lane. The oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision, and no police or Tesla statement is reported.

ai_role.statement: By Peters's account Autopilot braked and began a lane change to the right before he had seen the oncoming car. The TeslaCam footage, as described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving right while the wrong-way car veers off-road. The claim rests on the driver's statements and the footage. Neither Tesla nor police is quoted, and the oncoming driver's own swerve means the system's action cannot be shown to have been decisive.

fields.account: Before dawn on 27 February 2020, Bret Peters, a father and former state trooper, was driving his 2020 Tesla Model S on Autopilot. He was on Highway 49 near Cabarrus Arena in Concord, Cabarrus County, North Carolina. A car traveling the wrong way at about 60 mph came toward him in his lane. He wrote on Facebook that he did not see it until after Autopilot hit the brakes and started steering away. TeslaCam footage, aired by Fox 46 Charlotte and described by Electrek and the Daily Mail, shows the Tesla moving into the right lane. The oncoming car swerves onto the grassy median. There was no collision, and no police or Tesla statement is reported.
